about.title: Arvin Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Arvin families are often left facing funeral costs, lost income, and grief all at once. Public crash records show dozens of injury collisions occur each year on corridors like Comanche Drive and Tejon Highway, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday evenings. While recent city data shows no recorded traffic deaths in the latest reporting year, fatal collisions do still happen on Kern County roads, and when they do, California law gives certain surviving family members the right to pursue a civil wrongful death claim against the at-fault party. This is separate from any criminal case and focused on the financial and emotional losses left behind. We handle wrongful death claims for Arvin families on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. Our team can explain your options, evaluate the circumstances, and guide you through the claim process.

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, generally prioritizing a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. We can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options for your family.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California law allows recovery for lost financial support, lost household contributions, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, not just immediate expenses. Our team can help quantify what your family has actually lost.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. We can review your family's situation and confirm who is eligible to bring the claim.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family seeking financial recovery. Both can happen independently of one another.

items.question: Arvin's most recent crash data shows no traffic deaths, so why would we need this information?
items.answer: Public crash counts can shift from year to year, and the recorded data reflects only the most recent reporting period, not every year on roads like Bear Mountain Boulevard or Tejon Highway. If your family has lost someone in a collision, the two-year filing deadline still applies regardless of broader city statistics, so it's worth understanding your options early.
